_meta.spec: OVCA_Decision_Engine_Spec_v0.1 §4, extended for the agents that appear only in the clear cell, endometrioid and mucinous regimen records
_meta.hard_rule_2: Every rule below was read from the retrieved label text via the DailyMed SPL v2 API (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/services/v2/spls/{setid}.xml), fetched by tools/fetch_labels.py on 2026-10-05. No rule was reconstructed from memory. Only the Dosage and Administration (§2) modification tables and §4 Contraindications were read; Warnings (§5) were not extracted.
_meta.failed: sintilimab (no FDA label; not marketed in the United States, so no DailyMed SPL exists — see the sintilimab entry)
_meta.ctcae_version_warning: Label grade scales differ: CAMPTOSAR §2 uses NCI CTC v1.0; Oxaliplatin, XELODA, OPDIVO, YERVOY, IMFINZI, LENVIMA, IBRANCE use CTCAE (version not restated in §2). Grade thresholds are copied as printed.

irinotecan.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, CAMPTOSAR (irinotecan hydrochloride) injection [Pharmacia & Upjohn], SPL v37, effectiveTime 20260512, setid e518dfc6-7e93-4fee-a66c-51e1ab71c056
irinotecan.general_principle: §2.1/2.2: dose modifications are stepwise reductions (Dose Level −1, −2) based on the worst preceding toxicity; a new cycle should not begin until granulocytes ≥1500/mm³, platelets ≥100,000/mm³ and treatment-related diarrhoea has fully resolved; delay 1–2 weeks for recovery.

rules.action: consideration should be given to discontinuing therapy

rules.grade_threshold: prior pelvic/abdominal radiotherapy, performance status 2, or increased bilirubin
rules.action: consider starting one dose level lower

baseline_contraindications: known hypersensitivity to irinotecan or its excipients (§4)
irinotecan.notes: The CAMPTOSAR label carries no ovarian indication; JGOG3017 used irinotecan 60 mg/m² D1,8,15 q4w with cisplatin, a schedule not in the label. The §2 modification tables (NCI CTC v1.0) give dose-level reductions for diarrhoea, neutropenia and other non-haematologic toxicity; the table cells did not survive SPL text extraction and are not transcribed here.

oxaliplatin.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, Oxaliplatin injection, solution, concentrate [Hospira], SPL v18, effectiveTime 20260807, setid e51a62ba-d163-4c57-835c-8c86cf097e40
oxaliplatin.general_principle: §2.2: dose reduction to 75 mg/m² (adjuvant) or 65 mg/m² (advanced colorectal) for persistent G2 neuropathy, G4 neutropenia/febrile neutropenia, G3–4 thrombocytopenia or G3–4 GI toxicity after recovery.

rules.ae: interstitial lung disease or pulmonary fibrosis

rules.action: delay until neutrophils ≥1.5×10⁹/L and platelets ≥75×10⁹/L; reduce dose
after recovery reduce oxaliplatin and fluorouracil doses

baseline_contraindications: history of hypersensitivity reaction to oxaliplatin or other platinum-based drugs, including anaphylaxis (§4)
oxaliplatin.notes: Label indication is colorectal cancer; GOG-0241 used oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² q3w with capecitabine, a schedule not in the label. Prior carboplatin hypersensitivity is a §4 contraindication (other platinum-based drugs).

capecitabine.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, XELODA (capecitabine) tablet [H2-Pharma], SPL v32, effectiveTime 20260205, setid e702d84d-7162-4751-bf37-d724cc7e45a5
capecitabine.general_principle: §2.6 Table 1: withhold for grade 2–3 until grade 0–1, resume at 100/75/50% by appearance count; grade 4 → permanently discontinue or withhold and resume at 50%. Do not replace missed doses.

rules.action: PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE, or withhold until grade 0–1 and resume at 50%
resume once grade ≤2 (<3×ULN) at the Table 1 percentage
reduce starting dose to 75% (§2.7); CrCl <30: contraindicated by §2.7/§4 cross-reference

baseline_contraindications: history of severe hypersensitivity reaction to fluorouracil or capecitabine (§4)
capecitabine.notes: DPD deficiency warning lives in §5 (not extracted). GOG-0241 dose 850 mg/m² BID D1–14 q3w is below the label's colorectal 1250 mg/m² BID.

fluorouracil.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, Fluorouracil injection [Fresenius Kabi], SPL v7, effectiveTime 20260715, setid beb8c6c5-4b6e-4770-b6d4-718e33c7a2ff
fluorouracil.general_principle: §2.7: withhold for listed toxicities; resume at a reduced dose after improvement to grade 1 for diarrhoea, mucositis, myelosuppression or hand-foot syndrome; NO recommended resumption dose after cardiac toxicity, hyperammonaemic encephalopathy or acute cerebellar syndrome.

rules.ae: cardiac toxicity (angina, MI/ischaemia, arrhythmia, heart failure) in patients without prior CAD/myocardial dysfunction
rules.action: withhold; no recommended dose for resumption (effectively PERMANENT DISCONTINUATION)
withhold; no recommended dose for resumption

rules.ae: acute cerebellar syndrome / confusion / ataxia / visual disturbance
rules.action: withhold; no recommended dose for resumption
withhold; resume at reduced dose on improvement to grade 1
withhold; resume at reduced dose on improvement to grade 1
withhold; resume at reduced dose on improvement to grade 1
withhold; resume at reduced dose on improvement to grade 1

fluorouracil.notes: Used in the NTUH mFOLFOX6 template cited by the mucinous note; no ovarian indication.

nivolumab.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, OPDIVO (nivolumab) injection [E.R. Squibb & Sons], SPL v68, effectiveTime 20260812, setid f570b9c4-6846-4de2-abfa-4d0a4ae4e394
nivolumab.no_dose_reduction: §2.3: modification is WITHHOLD or PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE only. In combination with ipilimumab, withhold or permanently discontinue BOTH drugs for an adverse reaction meeting these guidelines.
nivolumab.general_principle: §2.3: withhold for severe (grade 3) immune-mediated reactions; permanently discontinue for life-threatening (grade 4) reactions, recurrent grade 3 reactions requiring systemic immunosuppression, or inability to reduce prednisone to ≤10 mg/day within 12 weeks of initiating steroids.

rules.action: withhold; PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE if no resolution within 12 weeks or steroids cannot be reduced

rules.grade_threshold: grade 4 (monotherapy); grade 3 or 4 in combination with ipilimumab

rules.ae: hepatitis, no tumour involvement of liver (combination with ipilimumab)
hepatitis, no tumour involvement of liver (monotherapy)

rules.action: withhold until clinically stable or PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE depending on severity

nivolumab.notes: Clear cell regimens (MoST-CIRCUIT, DART) are off-label; the OPDIVO label has no ovarian indication. Myocarditis handling is in §5 (not extracted); YERVOY §2.3 lists myocarditis grade 2–4 → permanent discontinuation.

ipilimumab.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, YERVOY (ipilimumab) injection [E.R. Squibb & Sons], SPL v47, effectiveTime 20260820, setid 2265ef30-253e-11df-8a39-0800200c9a66
ipilimumab.no_dose_reduction: §2.3: WITHHOLD or PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE only; with nivolumab, both drugs are withheld or discontinued together.
ipilimumab.general_principle: §2.3: permanently discontinue for grade 4 immune-mediated reactions, recurrent grade 3 reactions requiring systemic immunosuppression, persistent grade 2–3 reactions lasting ≥12 weeks after the last dose (excluding endocrinopathies), or inability to reduce prednisone to ≤10 mg/day within 12 weeks.

rules.ae: hepatitis, no tumour involvement of liver

rules.grade_threshold: grade 2–4 not improving to grade 1 within 2 weeks on topical therapy, or needing systemic treatment

ipilimumab.notes: MoST-CIRCUIT's one treatment-related death was immune-mediated myocarditis; the label's myocarditis rule is grade 2 → permanent discontinuation.

durvalumab.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, IMFINZI (durvalumab) injection [AstraZeneca], SPL v34, effectiveTime 20260831, setid 8baba4ea-2855-42fa-9bd9-5a7548d4cec3

rules.ae: hepatitis, no tumour involvement of liver

durvalumab.notes: Recorded for completeness: MOCCA durvalumab is a tier-7 record (not superior to chemotherapy), so these rules do not drive a ranking.

lenvatinib.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, LENVIMA (lenvatinib) capsule [Eisai], SPL v80, effectiveTime 20260630, setid f4bedd21-efde-44c6-9d9c-b48b78d7ed1e
lenvatinib.general_principle: §2.7 Table 1: withhold/reduce/discontinue by adverse reaction; Table 2 dose reductions for endometrial carcinoma 20 → 14 → 10 → 8 mg daily (the LARA starting dose was 20 mg).

rules.grade_threshold: grade 3 persisting despite optimal antihypertensive therapy
rules.action: withhold; resume at reduced dose when ≤grade 2
withhold until ≤2 g/24 h; PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE for nephrotic syndrome

rules.grade_threshold: >500 ms or >60 ms increase from baseline
rules.action: withhold until ≤480 ms or baseline; resume at reduced dose

lenvatinib.notes: Severe hepatic or renal impairment: reduced starting dose (§2.8–2.9). No ovarian indication; LARA used the endometrial-carcinoma dose with pembrolizumab.

letrozole.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, FEMARA (letrozole) tablet [Novartis], SPL v32, effectiveTime 20260611, setid 82b77d74-085f-45ac-a7dd-1f5c038bf406
baseline_contraindications: known hypersensitivity to letrozole or any excipient (§4)
letrozole.notes: §2 contains no dose-modification table (2.5 mg once daily; dose adjustment only for severe hepatic impairment, §2.4 not extracted). Ovarian use is off-label; the OEC regimen record extrapolates from PARAGON (anastrozole) and LACOG 1018 (letrozole + palbociclib).

anastrozole.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, ARIMIDEX (anastrozole) tablet [ANI Pharmaceuticals], SPL v12, effectiveTime 20260302, setid acbfaaa9-503c-4691-9828-76a7146ed6de
baseline_contraindications: demonstrated hypersensitivity to anastrozole or any excipient (anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria) (§4)
anastrozole.notes: §2 contains no dose-modification table (1 mg once daily). PARAGON used this dose off-label in ER/PR-positive recurrent ovarian cancer.

palbociclib.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, IBRANCE (palbociclib) tablet [U.S. Pharmaceuticals], SPL v11, effectiveTime 20260706, setid 89a142d5-7e61-48bf-9e77-e2cd124c4792
palbociclib.general_principle: §2.2: 125 → 100 → 75 mg/day; discontinue if a reduction below 75 mg/day would be required.

rules.grade_threshold: grade 3 with fever ≥38.5 °C and/or infection; grade 4 at any time
rules.action: withhold until recovery to grade ≤2; resume at next lower dose

rules.grade_threshold: grade ≥3 persisting despite optimal medical treatment
rules.action: withhold until grade ≤1 (or ≤2 if not a safety risk); resume at next lower dose

palbociclib.notes: Breast-cancer label; LACOG 1018 used 125 mg D1–21 q28d with letrozole in ovarian cancer off-label.

trastuzumab.source: FDA USPI via DailyMed, HERCEPTIN (trastuzumab) for injection [Genentech], SPL v27, effectiveTime 20260529, setid 492dbdb2-077e-4064-bff3-372d6af0a7a2

rules.grade_threshold: ≥16% absolute LVEF decrease from pre-treatment, or LVEF below institutional normal with ≥10% absolute decrease
rules.action: withhold ≥4 weeks; resume if LVEF returns to normal within 4–8 weeks with absolute decrease ≤15%

rules.grade_threshold: persistent (>8 weeks) LVEF decline, or dosing suspended on >3 occasions for cardiomyopathy

baseline_contraindications: none (§4); boxed warning for cardiomyopathy, infusion reactions, embryo-fetal toxicity and pulmonary toxicity (§5 not extracted)
trastuzumab.notes: Assess LVEF before and during treatment (§2.5). No ovarian indication; the mucinous evidence is a three-case series (McAlpine 2009).

sintilimab.source: No DailyMed SPL: sintilimab (Tyvyt) is approved by China's NMPA and is not FDA-approved; the FDA issued a complete response letter for its NSCLC application in 2022.
sintilimab.notes: INOVA's sintilimab + bevacizumab record therefore carries bevacizumab's label rules only. Anti-PD-1 class handling in the ranker uses the risk flags (ILD/pneumonitis, autoimmune disease) as trial exclusions, not label rules.
